title: Halloween week 2 (Shorts v4, Andrew): raven, ribbed newt, wheel bug + scorpion, burying beetle, luna moth deep dives
_note: Fill run 2026-10-25 (Studio + Postmaster) for the open Halloween-week slots 10/29-10/31. 3 YouTube Shorts at 20-25 s (raven, Iberian ribbed newt, wheel bug), claim-first; 3 TikTok deep dives at 61-75 s (scorpion UV glow, burying beetle, luna moth) with the open loop (promise in lines 1-3, two decoys, payoff at 50-80%; all pass tools/openloop.py). None of these animals appear in data/posted.csv or any earlier script. Meatball in jeopardy, lines 8 words or fewer, asks in character and never in the first 3 s, no quiz cards, no read-outs, every 'at' anchor a word. Voice en-US-AndrewMultilingualNeural +0% then atempo 1.10 (= +10%). Photos: iNaturalist research-grade, wild, CC0/CC BY (license confirmed via the API), whole animal, cut-outs checked by eye. Facts web-checked 10/25; sources on each hook beat.

beats.say: Ravens fake hiding their food. On purpose.
beats.short_title: Ravens Fake-Hide Their Food to Fool Thieves 🐦‍⬛
beats.comment: Has a bird ever outsmarted you? 👇
beats.bonus: Ravens have been seen sliding down snowbanks, apparently just for fun.
sources: Wikipedia, Common raven (learns to hide food out of sight of other ravens; 'pretending to make a cache without actually depositing the food', presumably to confuse onlookers; can mimic sounds including human speech; slides down snowbanks apparently for fun) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_raven (checked 2026-10-25)

Bugnyar & Kotrschal 2002, Animal Behaviour 64: 185-195, 'Observational learning and the raiding of food caches in ravens, Corvus corax: is it tactical deception?' (cachers delay caching and move caches when watched) — https://doi.org/10.1006/anbe.2002.3056
beats.caption: Ravens pretend to bury food when another raven is watching, then hide the real stash somewhere else. They can mimic human speech too. #raven #halloween #birds #animalfacts

beats.say: So I watched where one hid lunch.
It pretended to bury it.
Then hid the real food elsewhere.
Other ravens steal stashes all the time.
I went for the fake stash.
They can copy human speech too.
Great. It lies AND talks.
Like and follow. It's watching me.
Has a bird outsmarted you? Comment.
This newt stabs with its own ribs.
beats.short_title: This Newt Stabs With Its Own Ribs 🦴
beats.bonus: Iberian ribbed newts have been studied in space on at least six missions, starting in 1985.
sources: Wikipedia, Iberian ribbed newt (sharp ribs puncture through the stretched skin as a defense, causing little harm to the newt; milky, viscous poison secreted at the same time; pierced skin quickly regrows without infection; up to 30 cm in the wild; first sent to space in 1985 on Bion 7, studied on at least six missions) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iberian_ribbed_newt (checked 2026-10-25)

Heiss, Natchev, Salaberger, Gumpenberger, Rabanser & Weisgram 2010, Journal of Zoology 280: 156-162, 'Hurt yourself to hurt your enemy: new insights on the function of the bizarre antipredator mechanism in the salamandrid Pleurodeles waltl' — https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1469-7998.2009.00631.x
beats.caption: When something grabs an Iberian ribbed newt, it swings its ribs forward until the tips poke out through its skin, coated in poison. Then the skin heals. #newt #halloween #animalfacts #amphibians

beats.say: I offered it a hug anyway.
Grab it, and it swings its ribs forward.
The tips poke right through its skin.
Coated in poison on the way out.
So I grabbed it.
Its skin heals fast. Mine? Unclear.
It's also been to space. Six missions.
Way more than me.
Like and follow. Hugs are cancelled.
Would you hold one? Comment.
This bug wears a gear on its back.
beats.short_title: This Bug Wears a Gear and Drinks Its Prey ⚙️
beats.bonus: The wheel only appears after the final molt into an adult.
sources: Wikipedia, Arilus cristatus (North American wheel bug: dorsal crest shaped like a wheel or cog, appears only after the final molt; up to 38 mm; one of the largest terrestrial true bugs in North America; pins prey, plunges in its beak and injects enzymes, paralyzing it and dissolving its insides, then drains the fluids; bite generally considered more severe than the sting of common insects such as wasps; numbness can persist for days) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arilus_cristatus (checked 2026-10-25)
Wikipedia, Arilus (wheel bugs, named for the semicircular crest on the pronotum; generalist predators of insects) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arilus
beats.caption: The wheel bug, an assassin bug with a cog on its back, stabs prey with its beak, injects enzymes that dissolve the insides, then drinks them. Its bite can leave people numb for days. #wheelbug #assassinbug #halloween #insects

beats.say: It's called a wheel bug.
One of the biggest true bugs around.
I asked to borrow the wheel.
It stabs bugs with its beak.
Then melts their insides with spit.
And drinks them like a smoothie.
Its bite beats a wasp sting.
People stay numb for days.
Like and follow. I'm not a smoothie.
Bug soup: gross or genius? Comment.
Scorpions glow under a blacklight.
beats.loop_say: So the glow might be for seeing. Because
beats.short_title: Why Do Scorpions Glow Under a Blacklight? 🦂
beats.comment: What did you guess the glow was for? 👇
beats.bonus: About 25 of the 2,500+ scorpion species have venom that can kill a person; some species can go a year without eating.
sources: National Geographic (Ed Yong), 'Why do scorpions glow in the dark (and could their whole bodies be one big eye)?' (glow blue-green under UV; insects seem to avoid fluorescent scorpions; Gaffin: convert dim UV from moon and stars into blue-green, the colour they see best, 'the entire scorpion would effectively be one big eye'; Kloock overexposed scorpions to UV to use up the fluorescing chemicals, and scorpions that could still glow stuck to a sheltered area) — https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/article/why-do-scorpions-glow-in-the-dark-and-could-their-whole-bodies-be-one-big-eye (checked 2026-10-25)

Wikipedia, Scorpion (fluorescent chemicals such as beta-carboline in the cuticle; 'may function in detecting light'; over 2,500 described species; about 25 species have venom capable of killing a human; some survive up to a year without eating) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpion
Gaffin & Barker 2014, Journal of Arachnology 42: 111-118, 'Comparison of scorpion behavioral responses to UV under sunset and nighttime irradiances' — https://doi.org/10.1636/Hi12-91.1
beats.caption: Scorpions glow blue-green under UV light, and scientists still argue about why. It's not a lure: insects seem to avoid glowing scorpions. One idea: the whole body works like one big eye. #scorpion #halloween #blacklight #animalfacts

beats.say: Bright blue-green. Like a nightclub.
But nobody knows exactly why.
So I went to find out.
The glow lives in its shell.
A chemical in the outer layer.
Guess one: it lures in bugs?
Like a glowing snack sign.
Nope. Bugs seem to avoid glowing ones.
Guess two: a warning to predators?
Nobody has shown that works.
Here's the thing. It didn't warn me.
I poked it to check.
That was a sting, not a warning.
Tap like. I need the support.
Wait. What if the glow isn't for others?
What if it's for the scorpion?
Its whole body may work like one eye.
The glow turns faint moonlight blue-green.
The color its eyes see best.
Scientists wore out the glow on some.
The glowing ones stayed under shelter.
So it might be a night detector.
Still not proven. Science is ongoing.
Good news: only about twenty-five kinds are deadly.
Out of over twenty-five hundred species.
I still don't love those odds.
Bad news: I can't tell which.
Some go a whole year without eating.
I can't skip lunch.
Follow for more glowing nightmares.
Would you look with a blacklight? Comment.
This beetle steals dead mice.
beats.loop_say: So yes, the mouse is a nursery. Because
beats.short_title: Why This Beetle Buries Dead Mice 🪦
beats.bonus: The American burying beetle once lived in 35 US states; today it is found in about 9.
sources: Wikipedia, Burying beetle (antennae chemoreceptors detect a dead animal from a long distance; usually small birds or mice; dig under the carcass to bury it, about 8 hours; remove the hair; coat it with antibacterial and antifungal secretions; both parents raise the larvae; infanticide early on; American burying beetle listed 1989, once 35 states, now 9) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burying_beetle (checked 2026-10-25)

Missouri Department of Conservation, American burying beetle (smell dead animal carcasses from far away with organs on the antenna tips; crawl beneath it and dig the soil out; adults remain, guard their young and feed them regurgitated carrion; up to 1 1/4 inches) — https://mdc.mo.gov/discover-nature/field-guide/american-burying-beetle
beats.caption: Burying beetles smell a dead mouse from far away, bury it, strip the fur and coat it in germ-killing goo. It isn't lunch: it's a nursery, and both parents feed the babies. #buryingbeetle #halloween #insects #animalfacts

beats.say: But not to eat. Not exactly.
So I followed one to find out.
It's called a burying beetle.
Also called a sexton beetle. Like a gravedigger.
It's barely over an inch long.
It smells death from far away.
With sensors on its antennae.
Guess one: it's hiding lunch?
It digs under the mouse.
Until the mouse sinks underground.
That takes about eight hours.
I can't dig. I just roll.
Guess two: hiding it from flies?
It strips off all the fur.
Then coats it in germ-killing goo.
Wait. That's still not the reason.
I got way too close.
Tap like. I'm fine. Mostly.
Here's the thing. Two beetles move in.
A mom and a dad.
The mouse is a nursery.
The eggs hatch right next to it.
Both parents feed the babies.
Chewed-up mouse. Straight from their mouths.
It's a dead-mouse daycare.
Too many babies? They cull some.
Parenting is metal here.
One kind once lived in thirty-five states.
Now it's down to about nine.
I'm round and meaty. No naps outside.
If you see one, wave from far away.
Follow for more creepy parents.
Best or worst parents? Comment.
Luna moths have one huge problem.
beats.loop_say: So the problem was the mouth. Because
beats.short_title: The Luna Moth's One Huge Problem 🌙
beats.comment: What did you guess the problem was? 👇
beats.bonus: Luna moth caterpillars click as a warning and can throw up on attackers.
sources: Wikipedia, Luna moth (adults have vestigial mouthparts and do not feed; very brief 7-10 day adult lives, so rarely seen despite not being rare; wingspan typically ~114 mm and can exceed 178 mm (7.0 in); eyespots thought to confuse predators; larvae click as a warning and can regurgitate) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_moth (checked 2026-10-25)

Barber, Leavell, Keener, Breinholt, Chadwell, McClure, Hill & Kawahara 2015, PNAS 112(9): 2812-2816, 'Moth tails divert bat attack: evolution of acoustic deflection' (only 35% of intact luna moths were caught vs 81% with tails removed; spinning tails draw bat attacks) — https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1421926112
beats.caption: Luna moths spin their long tails to fool bats, and their eyespots spook predators. Their real problem: adults have no working mouth, never eat, and live about a week. #lunamoth #moth #halloween #animalfacts

beats.say: So I flew in to help.
Look at this thing. It's huge.
Pale green. Glowing. Very ghost-like.
Its wings can top seven inches.
Guess one: bats eat them?
Nope. Check out those long tails.
They spin while it flies.
So bats bite the tails instead.
With tails, only thirty-five percent got caught.
Tails clipped off? Eighty-one percent.
Guess two: those creepy eyespots?
Fake eyes that spook predators.
Here's the thing. That's a strength.
I tried to grab a wing.
Tap like. A moth just slapped me.
So what's the real problem?
Look closer at its face.
It has no working mouth.
Adult luna moths never eat.
They run on caterpillar leftovers.
So they only live about a week.
Seven to ten days. That's it.
That's why you almost never see one.
Even though they're not rare.
They're out there. Just not for long.
Find a mate. Lay eggs. Done.
No mouth. No snacks. Ever.
Honestly? My worst nightmare.
Bonus: the caterpillars click to warn you.
Then they throw up on attackers.
Basically a ghost with wings.
Follow for more spooky-cute bugs.
Would you trade your mouth for wings? Comment.
